title: NHANES 2015-2018, clinic pulse

population.description: Civilian, non-institutionalised US residents aged 18 and over who were examined, two survey cycles combined (2015-2016 and 2017-2018).
population.exclusions: None for medication (for example beta blockers), medical conditions, pregnancy, or an irregular pulse. Adults examined without a pulse reading are left out.

measurement.method: Pulse counted for 30 seconds by an examiner and doubled (NHANES variable BPXPLS).
measurement.device: Counted by an examiner; no device is recorded in this entry.
measurement.protocol: The participant rested quietly, seated, for 5 minutes, during the NHANES mobile examination centre visit.

analysis: Estimates use the examination sampling weights, halved for the two combined cycles. Percentiles are from the weighted empirical distribution.
95% intervals are from 500 bootstrap resamples of primary sampling units within strata (Rao-Wu), so they reflect the survey's clustered design.
No adjustment was made for examined adults without a pulse reading.
Subgroups with fewer than 50 people are not reported.
use_for: Sizing a study of clinic-measured pulse in US adults, by age, sex, and race and ethnicity.
Seeing the spread of a clinic pulse count in the general US adult population.
do_not_use_for: A reference for wearable resting heart rate: that is a different quantity. See the comparison of sources for this metric.
A healthy reference range: nobody was excluded for medication, medical conditions, pregnancy, or an irregular pulse.
caveats: **This is a clinic pulse, not a wearable resting heart rate.** Overnight or daily resting heart rate from a wearable is a different quantity, taken by a different method at a different time. Do not use these values as a reference for one.
**Values are even numbers.** A 30-second count doubled cannot be odd, so percentiles move in steps of 2 beats/min.
**This is the general population, not a healthy reference sample.** Nobody was excluded for medication (for example beta blockers), medical conditions, pregnancy, or an irregular pulse.
**Age 80 and over is one group** because NHANES records all such ages as 80.
**Race and ethnicity groups are NHANES's own categories**, self-reported.

citation.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, National Center for Health Statistics. National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey Data, 2015-2018. Hyattsville, MD: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.
citation.license: NCHS public-use data file. No licence name is stated; the NCHS terms (https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data_access/restrictions.htm) say users must "Use the data in this dataset for statistical reporting and analysis only."

verification: CDC's own reference report for 1999-2008 (Ostchega et al., National Health Statistics Reports no. 41) gives means of 71 beats/min for men and 74 for women aged 20 and over, in a sample that excluded conditions and medications affecting pulse. The values here, for a later period and with no exclusions, are 71.2 and 73.6. The report itself was read on 2026-10-06 (https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nhsr/nhsr041.pdf). Its abstract states: "females aged 20 and over have an RPR of 74 beats/min, SE 0.2, and males aged 20 and over have an RPR of 71 beats/min, SE 0.3", and "The mean RPR in adulthood plateaus at 72 beats/min".
